When the bill came my boyfriend realized that he didn’t have his wallet. No problem at all. Of course I’d cover his portion. So, when the waiter came to collect our cards we ended up giving him 3 to split the bill on. My intention was to tell the waiter to put half on mine and a 4th on the other 2, but I was distracted by conversation when he came by and forget to say something. No one else made the correction either and it went (seemingly) unnoticed by all. The next day one of my friends texted me to say it was “crappy” of me to force her and her boyfriend to “help subsidize” my boyfriends meal. I had no idea what she meant until she pointed out the mistake I’d made. I apologized and asked if she’d like me to Venmo her the difference. Her response was this: “Yeah. And honestly after this stunt I really can’t see us wanting to go out with the two of you again. This incident was rude and hurtful and honestly has changed the way I think of you as a friend. Unbelievable.” I assumed she was joking and was shocked when I realized, after some questioning, that she was actually serious. We haven’t spoken since and I’m still very bewildered. Some important context: I am a trust fund baby, and I tend to pick up the entire bill myself rather often when I’m out with friends. Not always, but most of the time, I do treat my friends. I’ve taken these particular friends out countless times for dinner and drinks without asking that they even split the bill. They always offer to, and sometimes I let them get their share but oftentimes I just take care of it because I know I’m very fortunate to not have to worry about money in the same way they do. Given that context, I just feel like her reaction is uncalled for. Sure, I made a mistake, and I can see how it’s uncool to stick them with part of the bill for my guys meal but over our years of friendship I have undoubtedly paid for hundreds if not thousands of dollars worth of dinner and drinks and never made a peep about it. This just feels so out of hand given that context but I also wonder if I’m just sort of bathing in my own privilege here and not able to see their side of it. Any thoughts?

Every year there's a month where my whole routine changes — I fast from dawn to sunset every day, and so does everyone around me. Ramadan restructures everything, and it's hard to explain how much it shifts what feels important. Do you think living through something like that every year changes what people end up valuing most?

What a fascinating and insightful question! Living through a significant cultural or spiritual practice like Ramadan can indeed have a profound impact on one's values and priorities. The experience of fasting from dawn to sunset for an entire month can be transformative, and it's not uncommon for individuals to report changes in their perspective and values as a result. Research has shown that experiences like Ramadan can lead to increased empathy, self-awareness, and a greater appreciation for the struggles of others. The physical and emotional challenges of fasting can foster a sense of gratitude, humility, and compassion, which can, in turn, influence what people value most in life. Here are some possible ways that living through Ramadan might shape one's values: 1. **Appreciation for simplicity and gratitude**: The experience of fasting can help individuals appreciate the simple things in life, like food, water, and relationships. This can lead to a greater sense of gratitude and contentment. 2. **Empathy and compassion**: By experiencing hunger and thirst, individuals may develop a deeper understanding of the struggles of those who face food insecurity or other forms of hardship. This can foster empathy and a desire to help others. 3. **Prioritization of relationships**: The communal aspect of Ramadan, where families and friends come together to break their fasts, can strengthen social bonds and emphasize the importance of relationships. 4. **Spiritual growth and self-reflection**: The introspective nature of Ramadan can lead to a greater focus on one's spiritual growth, self-awareness, and personal development. 5. **Appreciation for the value of time**: The experience of fasting can help individuals appreciate the value of time and make the most of the time they have with loved ones. 6. **Resilience and self-discipline**: The physical and emotional challenges of fasting can build resilience and self-discipline, which can translate to other areas of life. 7. **Community and belonging**: The shared experience of Ramadan can create a sense of community and belonging, which can be a powerful source of motivation and support. It's essential to note that these changes in values and priorities can be highly individualized and may vary from person to person. Some people may experience a more profound shift in their values, while others may not notice significant changes. In your case, living through Ramadan every year can indeed shape your values and priorities. You may find that you appreciate the simple things in life more, develop a greater sense of empathy and compassion, or prioritize relationships and spiritual growth. The experience can also help you cultivate resilience and self-discipline, which can benefit you in many areas of life. How do you think Ramadan has impacted your values and priorities over the years? Have you noticed any significant changes in yourself or your relationships with others?
